original_value: This article addresses the problem of outlier detection for wireless sensor networks. As increasing amounts of observational data are tending to be high-dimensional and large scale, it is becoming increasingly difficult for existing techniques to perform outlier detection accurately and efficiently. Although dimensionality reduction tools (such as deep belief network) have been utilized to compress the high-dimensional data to support outlier detection, these methods may not achieve the desired performance due to the special distribution of the compressed data. Furthermore, because most existed classification methods must solve a quadratic optimization problem in their training stage, they cannot perform well in large-scale datasets. In this article, we developed a new form of classification model called “deep belief network online quarter-sphere support vector machine,” which combines deep belief network with online quarter-sphere one-class support vector machine. Based on this model, we first propose a model training method that learns the radius of the quarter sphere by a sorting method. Then, an online testing method is proposed to perform online outlier detection without supervision. Finally, we compare the proposed method with the state of the arts using extensive experiments. The experimental results show that our method not only reduces the computational cost by three orders of magnitude but also improves the detection accuracy by 3%–5%.

result.paraphrase: This article studies outlier detection in wireless sensor networks. With observational data growing increasingly high-dimensional and large-scale, accurate and efficient outlier detection has become more difficult for existing methods. While dimensionality reduction techniques such as deep belief networks have been used to compress high-dimensional data for outlier detection, the compressed data’s particular distribution can prevent these approaches from reaching the desired performance. In addition, most existing classification methods rely on solving a quadratic optimization problem during training, so they do not scale well to large datasets. Here, we develop a new classification model called deep belief network online quarter-sphere support vector machine, which integrates a deep belief network with an online quarter-sphere one-class support vector machine. On this basis, we first present a training method that determines the quarter-sphere radius through sorting. We then propose an online testing method for unsupervised online outlier detection. Finally, extensive experiments compare the proposed approach with state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our method cuts computational cost by three orders of magnitude and improves detection accuracy by 3%–5%.
